title: Protocol to measure contraction, calcium, and action potential in human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes
protocol: Aspirate the medium from hiPSC-CMs cultured in 6-well plates.
Wash hiPSC-CMs twice with DPBS.
Incubate cells with Accutase (1 mL/well) for 6 min at 37°C.
Gently tap one side of the plate to agitate cells and improve dissociation efficiency.
Shake the plate gently after incubation, pipette solution several times to fully dissociate monolayer into single cells.
Transfer dissociated cell suspension into a 15 mL Falcon tube containing 8 mL of seeding medium.
Add 1 mL of seeding medium to the well and wash off remaining cells from the well.
Transfer washed cell suspension to the Falcon tube to give a final volume of 10 mL.
Remove the coating Matrigel from each well/dish/customized chamber.
Adjust the cell suspension to the density of 500,000 cells/mL in the seeding medium.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 10 mL reservoir.
Add 100 μL of the cell suspension to each well of the 96-well plate.
Mix 20 μL of cell suspension with 1:1 Trypan blue in a 0.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Transfer 15 μL of stained cell suspension in a Countess® Cell Counting Chamber Slide.
Count cell number by the Luna-FL automated fluorescence cell counter.
Use a multi-channel pipette to re-plate cells in a 96-well plate.
Pipette up and down several times before re-plating to avoid cells from settling.
Add 50 μL of cell suspension to each customized cell chamber on the coverslip for Ca2+ imaging.
Add 50 μL of seeding medium to each customized cell chamber on the coverslip for Ca2+ imaging.
Add 200 μL of cell suspension to each 35 mm glass-bottom dish for action potential measurement.
Add 300 μL of seeding medium to each 35 mm glass-bottom dish for action potential measurement.
Aspirate the seeding medium after 24 h.
Place a 1 mL non-filtered tip over the 2 mL aspiration pipette and ensure that the tip does not touch cells during aspiration.
Add 100 μL of hiPSC-CM culture medium to each well in a 96-well plate or customized cell chamber.
Replace the medium every other day until recording.
Add 500 μL of the hiPSC-CM culture medium to 35 mm glass-bottom dishes.
Replace the medium every other day until recording.
Put the 96-well plate on the plate holder.
Allow cells to stabilize for 5 minutes before recording.
Activate auto-focus and auto-brightness functions in the software interface.
Adjust the camera frame rate to 75 frames per second (fps).
Set the video/image format to 1024 × 1024 pixels.
Image the center of each well to avoid biased selection of a region of interest (ROI).
Ensure minimal vibration during recording.
Open the Sony SI8000 cardiac analysis software.
Conduct motion detection and analyses automatically.
Detect contraction start, contraction peak, contraction end, relaxation peak, and relaxation end for each beating cycle.
Prepare Tyrode’s solution as described in the materials and equipment section.
Prepare Fura-2 AM loading solution as described in the materials and equipment section.
Aspirate the culture medium in customized cell chambers.
Wash hiPSC-CMs twice with 100 μL of Tyrode’s solution.
Load 100 μL of Fura-2 AM loading solution to hiPSC-CMs in the customized cell chambers.
Incubate the hiPSC-CMs at room temperature for 10 min.
Remove Fura-2 AM loading solution from the hiPSC-CMs.
Wash twice with 100 μL of Tyrode’s solution.
Incubate the hiPSC-CMs in Tyrode’s solution for another 5 min at room temperature to allow de-esterification of Fura-2 AM.
Put the coverslips in the magnetic heated platform.
Remove tubes on the coverslip and put the narrow bath chamber with grease at the bottom on top of the coverslip.
Secure the bath chamber in place using the magnetic clamps and ensure there is no leak.
Add 1 mL of Tyrode’s solution into the chamber.
Add a drop of immersion oil on the objective.
Place the magnetic heated platform in a stage adapter on the stage of an inverted epifluorescence microscope equipped with a 40× oil immersion objective.
Put the temperature sensor in the bath chamber.
Set the temperature controller at 37°C.
Connect the field stimulation electrodes with a stimulator.
Set the field stimulation at 0.5 Hz with a pulse duration of 20 ms.
Excite Fura-2 AM loaded cells with Lambda DG 4 ultra-high-speed wavelength switching light source at both 340 and 380 nm in fast-switching mode.
Collect emission fluorescence signals at 510 nm with the iXon Ultra 897 EMCCD camera.
Find a region of interest under the eye pieces first.
Switch to the live view by camera.
Ensure cells are focused under the live view by camera.
Click “Run now” to start recording under the ND Acquisition mode in NIS Elements AR software.
Set exposure time for each wavelength at 20 ms and total recording time at 20 s.
Three days before imaging, prepare the lentivirus infection medium as described in materials and equipment.
Add 300 μl of prepared medium to each dish with an MOI of three.
Use the minimum required volume for infection to improve efficiency.
After 24 hours, aspirate the infection medium.
Add 500 μL of hiPSC-CM culture medium to each dish until imaging.
On the day of imaging, turn on the confocal microscope and incubation system.
Maintain the temperature of the imaging chamber at 37°C and humidify it to avoid evaporation during imaging.
Remove the medium from the dish.
Wash cells twice with 1 mL of Tyrode’s solution.
Remove the washing solution.
Add 1 mL of Tyrode’s solution to the dish.
Place the dish onto a holding adapter for stabilization for 5 minutes before imaging.
Perform live-cell imaging using an inverted Zeiss LSM 710 confocal microscope equipped with a 20× objective (NA: 0.8).
Use the line-scan mode for measuring the action potential of single cells.
Allow cells to adapt to Tyrode’s solution before imaging.
Start live cell imaging in a line scan mode with an excitation wavelength of 488 nm and emission filtered between 493–630 nm.
Select the scanning line across the cell membrane at maximal scanning speed.
Set the image size to 512 × 1 pixels and record for 8 seconds.
Conduct recordings using Zen software, saving images as LSM files.
Open line-scan images in ImageJ.
Invert fluorescence intensity using the Invert function under Edit.
Select the entire image (Ctrl+A).
Plot the profile of the image (Ctrl+Alt+K) to determine amplitude and action potential duration at 30%, 50%, 70%, and 90%.
Adjust the recording time according to cell beating speed for multiple cycle recordings.
